title: 1. Made a game that took me almost a year 2. Used AI to generate visual assets. Code, story and mechanics are my own 3. Disclosed the AI use in the game page and inside the actual game 4. Game gets called AI slop when they saw the disclosure, without even playing the demo
author: stopstopstoptopopp
selftext:
How do you even deal with these people? I know they're like 10% of the commenters, most are positive, but it's just frustrating.

How insecure must they feel to leave degrading comments on a game not that even popular?

I thought that letting people know that the visual assets are made with AI will make those kind of people leave it alone. Apparently not.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: You don’t deal with them, you ignore them and focus on people that have constructive criticism or like your game

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
Link to the game please,  so we can judge you too
It doesn't matter what you disclaim, if it looks like generic ai, ppl will know. Getting a good art direction and staying on that direction with ai is really hard

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Du hast eine lustige Mischung aus zwei ui designen. Das helle und das im viewport mittig. Das Innere gefällt mir besser taucht aber sonst nicht auf. 
Links am Rande steht sehr skurriler Text. Nicht nur zu viel Text sondern komisches Zeichen. 
Deine Figuren sehen cool aus aber sind inhaltlich sehr wild, möglich dass das in die Story passt, weiß ich nicht. 

Ich habe es nicht gespielt aber es wirkt auf mich als ob du die ersten 50% geschafft hast. Was dir fehlt ist die zweite Hälfte, polish polish polish. 
Nimm dir die Zeit und Versuch ein einheitliches Design zu schaffen, mein Tipp. 

Vorschlag
Mach nicht einen Rahmen und ein Spiel sondern schau dass die sidebar Infos im eigentlichen Spiel sichtbar sind am besten als Teil der Welt. Zb eine Tafel im Hintergrund die als Lob funktioniert

replies.author: mimendalerenda_Lab
replies.body:
justo he estado trabajando en esos detalles.    
la intención gráfica de mi juego es que muestre dos "mundo" simultáneamente (lo real y lo que es resultado de su mente).

En cuanto a la interfaz grafica, he estado trabajando en conseguir que el marco se lea como una carpeta clasificadora.

Lo del volumen de texto, se que me he pasado, pero mi juego va sobre recuperar libros viejos y medio olvidados, por eso, una parte de lo que se lee es el texto del libro que estas "reconstruyendo" para que no se pierda. y luego un montón mas de textos por todas partes que se lee como una sobrecarga sensorial, que es lo que esta padeciendo el protagonista del juego. 

Gracias por tu comentario, poco  a poco lo dejaré polished polished polished

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body: Die Idee Wesen aus alten Büchern / aus märchen ist super! Bau die Idee weiter aus. Gestalte die Welt wie ein Märchenbuch

replies.author: PhilosophyforOne
replies.body:
I think part of the problem might be that the game description is clearly written with AI. So the first reaction is "this is probably AI-slop". 

I mean, as I read through what it actually says, the concept gets more compelling. But phrases like "Here, every hand you win is a line of their book brought back into existence, a page that isn't forgotten, a book that doesn't die." are so very recognizably AI that they devalue the content of the description.

Try to rework your marketing. Write it out in your own words, and see if you can land somewhere. I dont think the problem is the content, it's more the AI-traces in the packaging. 

But yes, the hate is also real. Good luck though!

replies.body: Even the very first short description has the infinitely memed —

replies.body: Yeah game description is a level of lazy that makes this a bit sus

comments.author: This-Memory4929
comments.body:
Hi! One thing I’ve learned, though, is that if you look at the numbers instead of the comments, the most critical people are often simply the loudest. People who don’t have a problem with the use of AI, or who maybe find the game interesting, often don’t comment at all. They watch the trailer, try the demo, wishlist the game, and move on.
Unfortunately, trying to convince these people is a battle against windmills. If the game is good, it will find its place.
Good luck!

comments.author: cowman3456
comments.body:
Nah man, the anti-AIs will attack you with all the fervor of a MAGA encountering a gender neutral restroom.  Hate first, justify at any cost later.

comments.author: throwaway275275275
comments.body: Ok but what did you expect ? Disclosing that you used AI doesn't make it free of AI, the haters of AI will hate it. They don't hate "lack of disclosure", they hate AI. The only way to make those people like your game is either not use AI or use AI and don't disclose it, and if the game is good they'll like it.
